why: Advice 1 gets the call right and gets the economics right: annual billing breaks even at roughly 3% monthly churn. It also covers practical gaps like a refund policy, procurement needs and delayed price increases. Advice 2 has sharper deadlines and success metrics, but some of its logic is shaky: it says to drop the discount if buyers 'would have paid $588 anyway', and it judges success on whether adopters are new customers, even though the 40 who asked are probably loyal ones. It also invents cutoffs like '10+ switches' without explaining them.
